notes: Legacy remains the default runtime until Stage 12.
Rewrite uses a fresh database and does not migrate legacy SQLite or uploads.
The React home and minimal canvas receiver implementations are complete; authenticated end-to-end integration remains covered by the local Docker blocker.
The machine-readable work-package catalog is authoritative for scope, checks, acceptance, blockers, and successors.
Risk-tiered verification derives affected workspaces from staged paths; full repository check/build remains mandatory at stage and release gates and before a mid-stage push.
Rewrite-only visual polish is constrained by react-visual-delta-allowlist.json; Legacy remains read-only.
The concentrated React home and minimal canvas polish pass is complete with named Lucide imports, reduced-motion-safe micro interactions, responsive visual evidence, and no Legacy mutation.
The rewrite capability registry and /api/v1/capabilities expose credential-free readiness; production actions remain fail-closed unless a capability is verified.
Identity provider contracts use deterministic development implementations and production fail-closed placeholders; real provider delivery, OAuth callbacks, and live verification remain deferred.
Moderation, notification, and audit records now have workspace-scoped PostgreSQL persistence, idempotency keys, retry timestamps, and worker recovery seams; real external providers remain deferred.

Billing domain foundation now defines integer-fen money, explicit order/payment/subscription state machines, and durable catalog/order/payment/subscription/entitlement/refund/invoice/event tables; merchant integrations remain deferred.

Payment provider contracts now fail closed in production and cover checkout, query, refund, renewal mandate, webhook signature verification, and provider-scoped replay protection; merchant credentials remain deferred.
Rewrite commercial routes now provide pricing, account, billing, credits, security, and data pages with existing account-menu entry points; unavailable services remain visibly fail-closed.
Compliance routes and the data-rights request foundation now cover legal notice, reporting, appeal, export, deletion, and closure seams; approvals and real processors remain release blockers.
Canvas document persistence now has a registered-node allowlist, explicit serializer, and snapshot migration registry; temporary and unknown nodes cannot be persisted as restored business nodes.
Stage 3.5 builds fail-closed SaaS provider, commercial, and compliance foundations before full canvas migration.
The legacy runtime remains the default and is unchanged.
